name: Sign-in
note: The aside's tagline and sub-line are SR-5. The three error rows after the generic one (S-05.04, S-05.05 and S-05.16) are for the implementation's status mapping: today every failure shows the one generic message.
rows: The display line states the task (Richards); the wordmark follows it. No greeting that assumes a returning user.
Use the email address linked to your Kiwi account.
Says what to enter instead of a claim about the product (C16).

rows.o: Login failed. Please check your credentials and try again.
rows.fix: Try again, or ask your administrator if it keeps happening.
rows.m: Login failed. Please check your credentials and try again.
rows.t: The fallback only. It ships together with the status mapping (S-05.04 for a refused sign-in, S-05.05 for no response, S-05.16 for a server error), never alone: without the mapping a wrong password would be told that the server did not respond as expected, a cause the page does not know. It states the one cause the page can always state, the closed generic line (§ Errors), for a failure that matches no mapping row, and a fix that fits a cause nobody knows: try again, then ask the administrator if it keeps happening. The hint to check the email and password stays in S-05.04, where the response says the credentials were refused.

rows.why: That email and password don't match.
rows.fix: Check both and try again, or ask your administrator to reset your password.
rows.m: Login failed. Please check your credentials and try again.
rows.t: For the implementation: the wording when the response is a refused sign-in. It says what happened first, like its siblings S-05.03, S-05.05 and S-05.16 (the alert is a form-level message, `Login.tsx:161-166`, not a field's error state, so the input-error form does not apply), then the cause the page can state for a refused sign-in, then what to do. Ships with S-05.03 and the rest of the status mapping, so that S-05.03 is only what is left for a failure no mapping row matches.

rows.m: Login failed. Please check your credentials and try again.
rows.t: For the implementation: the wording when no response arrived.

rows.o: Your session has expired. Please log in again.
rows.m: Your session has expired. Please log in again.
rows.t: Ships with or after the access-control merge (branch `fix/access-control`): there a signed-in user who may not do something gets a 403 and the web client keeps the sign-in on a 403 (defect B2). Until that merges, a refused permission also lands here with this text, so "Your sign-in has expired" would be wrong for it. A refused permission uses the no-permission copy (DS.29, DS.30) or the page's own `denied` error.

rows: One verb pair: sign in and sign out.

Capitals typed into the string. Two test lines query it: `Login.test.tsx:123` (`getByText("OR")`, with Google sign-in on) fails after the change, and `Login.test.tsx:106` (`queryByText("OR")` is absent in the password-only case) would pass vacuously, because a query for the old capitals finds nothing in the new text. The pair must discriminate: `queryByText("or")` absent in the default case (:106) and `getByText("or")` present with Google sign-in on (:123), and `queryByText("OR")` absent in both, which proves the capitals are gone. The divider is a conjunction between two controls, so it stays lowercase (the C1 first-letter lint is waived for it).

rows.t: The variant for a configured support address (C17): the source builds this text from its first sentence and, when `SUPPORT_EMAIL` is set, " Please contact {SUPPORT_EMAIL}." (`GoogleRedirectHandler.tsx:57`), so this row's Old is the whole text of that reading and S-07.04's is the reading without it. The page cannot tell whether Google withheld the address or the response left it out (`GoogleRedirectHandler.tsx:27`, `:35`), so the cause line says only that it was not available.

name: Not found
note: The mascot (the standing bird) sits above the heading; the rest is these four strings. Inserted under the plan's never-dead-end constraint (an error or a not-found page always gives a way on, Yifrah): the two way-back controls, "Go to your classes" and "Sign in", are links to routes that already exist (`/` for a signed-in visitor, `/login` for a signed-out one), so they add no route and no region. They are the one piece of navigation this page gains, and the Stage 1 hooks line above ("no region, route or navigation may be added") is read as no new destination.
